ATP.clue: Nucleotide that drives the sodium-potassium pump and is exhausted early in ischemia
ATP.rationale: Oxidative phosphorylation supplies most of this nucleotide. Ischemia stops the pump, sodium enters, and cells swell.

PCR.clue: Method that copies a chosen nucleic-acid sequence with a heat-stable polymerase
PCR.rationale: Taq polymerase survives the denaturation step. The test amplifies DNA or, after reverse transcription, RNA.

GFR.clue: Filtration rate measured exactly with inulin and estimated from creatinine
GFR.rationale: Inulin is freely filtered and neither reabsorbed nor secreted. Creatinine slightly overestimates the rate because tubules secrete it.

DNA.clue: Genetic polymer whose ultraviolet thymine dimers are removed by nucleotide excision repair
DNA.rationale: Xeroderma pigmentosum is a failure of that repair and leads to skin cancers. Mismatch repair failure is the Lynch pathway instead.

RNA.clue: Genome type of influenza, HIV, and poliovirus, unlike herpesviruses
RNA.rationale: Positive-sense RNA can act as a message. Retroviruses reverse-transcribe their RNA before integrating.

TSH.clue: Pituitary signal that is the first blood test when thyroid function is in doubt
TSH.rationale: High levels with low thyroid hormone mean primary hypothyroidism. Low levels with high thyroid hormone suggest pituitary failure or exogenous hormone.

ACTH.clue: Pituitary peptide that drives cortisol and is high when the adrenal glands fail
ACTH.rationale: Primary adrenal failure has high levels and hyperpigmentation. Exogenous glucocorticoids suppress it, so stopping them suddenly can cause crisis.

ADH.clue: Posterior pituitary hormone that inserts water channels when plasma osmolality rises
ADH.rationale: It acts on V2 receptors of principal cells and also raises urea permeability in the inner medulla. Very low blood volume overrides osmolality and still triggers release.

PTH.clue: Hormone that raises serum calcium, lowers phosphate, and is anabolic only in pulses
PTH.rationale: Continuous excess resorbs bone. Once-daily analog therapy builds bone because of that timing difference.

ACE.clue: Lung-endothelium enzyme that makes angiotensin II and breaks down bradykinin
ACE.rationale: Inhibitors raise bradykinin, which explains cough and angioedema. Macrophages in sarcoidosis also express the enzyme, so the serum level can rise.

EPO.clue: Kidney hormone increased by hypoxia and secreted by some renal cell carcinomas
EPO.rationale: It drives red-cell production. Inappropriate secretion also occurs with cerebellar hemangioblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma.

TNF.clue: Macrophage cytokine of fever, cachexia, and septic shock, and the target of several biologics
TNF.rationale: It also maintains granulomas, so blockers can reactivate tuberculosis. Screen for latent TB before starting those drugs.

HIV.clue: Retrovirus that enters CD4 cells through CD4 plus CCR5 or CXCR4
HIV.rationale: Reverse transcriptase, integrase, and protease are drug targets. The CD4 count falls and opportunistic infections follow.

CMV.clue: Herpesvirus with owl-eye inclusions and the most common congenital viral infection
CMV.rationale: Congenital disease causes periventricular calcifications, hearing loss, and blueberry-muffin rash. In advanced HIV it causes retinitis and linear esophageal ulcers.

EBV.clue: Herpesvirus that binds CD21 and drives heterophile-positive mononucleosis
EBV.rationale: It is linked to Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Cytotoxic T cells are the atypical lymphocytes, and the spleen can rupture.

HPV.clue: Nonenveloped DNA virus whose E6 and E7 proteins disable p53 and Rb
HPV.rationale: Types 16 and 18 cause cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. Types 6 and 11 cause warts and recurrent respiratory papillomas.

HSV.clue: Virus latent in sensory ganglia that causes hemorrhagic temporal-lobe encephalitis
HSV.rationale: Cowdry inclusions and multinucleated giant cells are histologic clues. Acyclovir must be activated by viral thymidine kinase.

DKA.clue: Anion-gap acidosis with hyperglycemia and ketones, mostly in insulin deficiency
DKA.rationale: Total-body potassium is low even when the serum level is high. Insulin drives potassium inward, so potassium is replaced as treatment proceeds.

TTP.clue: Pentad of thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, neurologic change, fever, and renal injury from ultra-large von Willebrand multimers
TTP.rationale: ADAMTS13 is deficient, often from an autoantibody. Plasma exchange is the treatment, and platelets are not routinely transfused.

DIC.clue: Consumptive coagulopathy with low fibrinogen, high D-dimer, prolonged clotting times, and schistocytes
DIC.rationale: Triggers include sepsis, trauma, amniotic-fluid embolus, and acute promyelocytic leukemia. Replace fibrinogen and treat the cause.

PNH.clue: Acquired loss of the GPI anchor so red cells lack CD55 and CD59 and lyse
PNH.rationale: A PIGA mutation in a stem cell is the cause. Thrombosis in unusual veins is the leading threat, and a C5 inhibitor raises Neisseria risk.

RAS.clue: Proto-oncogene GTPase stuck active in many pancreatic and colon cancers
RAS.rationale: It normally turns itself off by hydrolyzing GTP. A point mutation blocks that hydrolysis and locks growth signaling on.

MYC.clue: Transcription-factor oncogene translocated next to immunoglobulin genes in Burkitt lymphoma
MYC.rationale: The classic translocation is t(8;14). The tumor has a starry-sky pattern of macrophages among dark lymphocytes.

APC.clue: Tumor suppressor that holds beta-catenin for destruction and is lost in familial polyposis
APC.rationale: Hundreds of colorectal adenomas follow, and cancer is nearly certain without colectomy. The gene sits on chromosome 5.

VHL.clue: Tumor suppressor that normally lets HIF be degraded, lost in cerebellar and renal tumors
VHL.rationale: Clear-cell renal carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and hemangioblastomas define the syndrome. HIF-driven VEGF explains the vascular tumors.

PKU.clue: Deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase causing musty odor and intellectual disability if untreated
PKU.rationale: Tyrosine becomes essential. A strict diet is required, including during pregnancy to prevent fetal injury.

NPH.clue: Gait apraxia, urinary incontinence, and dementia with intermittently high ventricular pressure
NPH.rationale: Arachnoid granulations fail to absorb CSF. Large-volume tap or shunting can improve gait.

LPS.clue: Gram-negative outer-membrane lipid that triggers macrophages to release TNF and IL-1
LPS.rationale: Lipid A is the toxic moiety. The result is fever, hypotension, and disseminated coagulation, classically in meningococcemia.

NAC.clue: Antidote that restores glutathione so the toxic acetaminophen metabolite can be conjugated
NAC.rationale: The liver injury is centrilobular because that zone is richest in CYP2E1. Give the antidote as early as possible, and it still helps later.

PTU.clue: Thionamide that blocks thyroid peroxidase and also peripheral conversion of T4 to T3
PTU.rationale: It is preferred in thyroid storm and in the first trimester. Severe hepatitis and agranulocytosis are the dangerous adverse effects.

IGA.clue: Mucosal antibody missing in the most common primary immunodeficiency
IGA.rationale: Many people are asymptomatic. Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis during transfusion, and IgA deficiency can make celiac serology falsely negative.

CCK.clue: Duodenal hormone released by fat and protein that contracts the gallbladder and relaxes the sphincter of Oddi
CCK.rationale: It also slows gastric emptying and stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion. I cells are the source.

SHH.clue: Signaling protein whose failure causes holoprosencephaly and cyclopia
SHH.rationale: The same pathway is involved in patterning of the limbs and neural tube. Patau syndrome is a classic association of the brain defect.

ALS.clue: Combined upper and lower motor neuron loss without sensory loss
ALS.rationale: Anterior horn cells and the corticospinal tract both degenerate. Riluzole decreases glutamate excitotoxicity.

CFTR.clue: Chloride channel lost in the chromosome 7 disease of thick mucus and salty sweat
CFTR.rationale: The common folding mutation is degraded in the endoplasmic reticulum. Lungs grow Pseudomonas, the pancreas fails, and the vas deferens may be absent.

BRCA.clue: Homologous-recombination genes whose loss raises breast, ovarian, prostate, and pancreatic cancer risk
BRCA.rationale: PARP inhibitors exploit the repair failure. Prophylactic surgery is considered for high-risk carriers.

DOWN.clue: Trisomy 21 pattern of endocardial cushion defects, duodenal atresia, and early Alzheimer disease
DOWN.rationale: Brushfield spots, a single palmar crease, and Hirschsprung disease are associated. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia risk is increased.

AUER.clue: Needle crystals of fused granules in myeloid blasts, especially the promyelocytic subtype
AUER.rationale: They are myeloperoxidase positive. The promyelocytic leukemia can present with disseminated coagulation and responds to all-trans retinoic acid.

LEWY.clue: Alpha-synuclein inclusion of Parkinson disease and a dementia with visual hallucinations
LEWY.rationale: The substantia nigra pars compacta loses pigmented neurons. Typical antipsychotics worsen the motor disease.

PICK.clue: Frontotemporal dementia with round tau inclusions and early personality change
PICK.rationale: Knife-edge frontal and temporal atrophy is the gross clue. Memory is relatively spared at the start, unlike typical Alzheimer disease.

RETT.clue: MECP2 disorder of girls who regress, wring their hands, and lose purposeful movement
RETT.rationale: It is X-linked dominant and usually lethal in boys. Development is normal for the first months.

CORI.clue: Debranching-enzyme glycogenosis with limit-dextrin accumulation and milder hypoglycemia
CORI.rationale: Hepatomegaly and hypotonia occur. The liver cannot fully dismantle glycogen branches.

BITE.clue: Red-cell shape left when the spleen pits out denatured hemoglobin in oxidative hemolysis
BITE.rationale: The trigger is often infection, sulfa, primaquine, dapsone, or fava beans. The enzyme assay can look normal during the acute hemolysis.

CONN.clue: Aldosterone-secreting adenoma with hypertension, hypokalemia, and low renin
CONN.rationale: Metabolic alkalosis accompanies the potassium loss. The aldosterone-renin ratio is high, unlike secondary hyperaldosteronism.

POTT.clue: Tuberculous osteomyelitis of the spine that can collapse a vertebra and form a cold abscess
POTT.rationale: Hematogenous spread reaches the vertebral body. Cord compression is the feared complication.

GHON.clue: Calcified focus of primary tuberculosis plus its hilar node
GHON.rationale: Primary infection usually sits in the mid or lower lobe. Secondary reactivation prefers the apex, where oxygen tension is higher.

LYME.clue: Ixodes-borne spirochete illness with erythema migrans, AV block, facial palsy, and a late knee arthritis
LYME.rationale: Borrelia burgdorferi does not stain well on Gram stain. Doxycycline is usual early treatment; meningitis or carditis needs a cephalosporin.

AIRE.clue: Thymic transcription factor required to show self-antigens during negative selection
AIRE.rationale: Mutation causes chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, and adrenal failure. That triad is autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1.

COAL.clue: Upper-lobe pneumoconiosis of miners, with black pigment and a risk of massive fibrosis
COAL.rationale: Rheumatoid nodules in this dust disease are Caplan syndrome. Simple anthracosis is the milder macrophage pigment load.

BOHR.clue: Right shift of the oxygen curve when carbon dioxide and hydrogen ions rise in working tissue
BOHR.rationale: Unloading of oxygen is easier. Fetal hemoglobin and carbon monoxide shift the curve the other way.

FICK.clue: Cardiac-output calculation from oxygen consumption divided by the arteriovenous oxygen difference
FICK.rationale: It is the physiologic basis of some thermodilution concepts. Output rises when tissues extract more oxygen for a given arterial content.

DLCO.clue: Gas-transfer measurement that falls in emphysema and fibrosis but stays normal in asthma
DLCO.rationale: It also falls in anemia and rises in pulmonary hemorrhage and polycythemia. Chronic bronchitis alone does not destroy alveolar surface the way emphysema does.

VASA.clue: Fetal vessels crossing the internal os that rupture when the membranes break
VASA.rationale: Bleeding is painless and the fetal heart rate falls. The blood is fetal, unlike maternal bleeding in placenta previa.

BUDD.clue: Hepatic-vein thrombosis with tender hepatomegaly, ascites, and a hypercoagulable source
BUDD.rationale: Polycythemia, pregnancy, and hepatocellular carcinoma are classic causes. Centrilobular congestion is the histologic result.

WEST.clue: Model in which the lung base is continuously perfused and the apex is intermittent
WEST.rationale: Both blood flow and ventilation are higher at the base, but flow increases more, so the ventilation-perfusion ratio is higher at the apex.

KEHR.clue: Referred shoulder pain from blood or pus irritating the diaphragm
KEHR.rationale: Splenic rupture and hemoperitoneum are classic causes. The phrenic nerve shares cervical roots with shoulder sensation.

PEAU.clue: Dimpled breast skin from dermal lymphatic blockage by inflammatory carcinoma
PEAU.rationale: This is a clinical diagnosis of locally advanced cancer, not an infection. It needs urgent systemic therapy rather than drainage.

PICA.clue: Appetite for ice, clay, or starch that often signals iron deficiency
PICA.rationale: In adults, iron deficiency means blood loss until proven otherwise. Hookworm and celiac disease are other causes.

REID.clue: Ratio of bronchial gland thickness to wall thickness that exceeds one half in chronic bronchitis
REID.rationale: The clinical definition is a productive cough for three months in two successive years. Hypoxemia and cor pulmonale come earlier than in pure emphysema.

GVHD.clue: Donor T cells attacking host skin, liver, and gut after a marrow transplant
GVHD.rationale: Irradiating cellular blood products prevents a similar reaction in immunocompromised recipients. It is a type IV process.

CVID.clue: Later-onset hypogammaglobulinemia with normal B-cell counts, sinopulmonary infections, and lymphoma risk
CVID.rationale: Both sexes are affected, unlike Bruton disease. Autoimmunity and granulomatous disease are common.

COPD.clue: Airflow obstruction from smoking that combines small-airway disease and alveolar destruction
COPD.rationale: The FEV1/FVC ratio is low. Long-term supplemental oxygen improves survival when resting hypoxemia persists.

ARDS.clue: Noncardiogenic edema with hyaline membranes and a normal pulmonary-capillary wedge pressure
ARDS.rationale: Sepsis, aspiration, trauma, and pancreatitis are triggers. Low-tidal-volume ventilation reduces further lung injury.

AIDS.clue: CD4 count below 200 or an opportunistic illness that defines advanced HIV, such as esophageal candidiasis or pneumocystis pneumonia
AIDS.rationale: Combination antiretroviral therapy suppresses viral load and restores immune function. Prophylaxis is chosen according to the CD4 threshold.

LCIS.clue: Incidental lobular proliferation that marks bilateral breast-cancer risk but is not itself invasive
LCIS.rationale: E-cadherin is lost, as in invasive lobular carcinoma. It usually does not calcify and is not a surgical emergency.

DCIS.clue: Malignant cells inside breast ducts that have not crossed the basement membrane
DCIS.rationale: Comedo necrosis and microcalcifications mark higher-grade lesions. Nipple Paget disease is this process reaching the epidermis.

MRKH.clue: 46,XX absence of the uterus with normal ovaries, normal pubic hair, and a blind vagina
MRKH.rationale: Androgen action is intact, which separates it from androgen-insensitivity syndrome. Ovaries are present, so secondary sexual characteristics develop.

GOLGI.clue: Organelle that packages proteins and is the site of mannose-6-phosphate tagging for lysosomes
GOLGI.rationale: I-cell disease fails that tagging step, so lysosomal enzymes are secreted. N-linked glycosylation begins in the endoplasmic reticulum and is finished here.

FABRY.clue: X-linked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency with angiokeratomas, neuropathic pain, and renal failure
FABRY.rationale: Ceramide trihexoside accumulates. Heart, kidney, and early stroke are the life-limiting problems.

POMPE.clue: Lysosomal acid maltase deficiency with cardiomegaly and severe hypotonia
POMPE.rationale: Glycogen is trapped inside lysosomes, including in cardiac muscle. It is the glycogenosis that behaves like a lysosomal storage disease.

TARUI.clue: Muscle phosphofructokinase deficiency with cramps, myoglobinuria, and hemolysis
TARUI.rationale: Exercise does not raise venous lactate, as in McArdle disease. Red cells also need this enzyme, so they hemolyze.

ICELL.clue: Storage disease in which lysosomal enzymes lack mannose-6-phosphate and spill into the blood
ICELL.rationale: Inclusion bodies fill fibroblasts. Coarse facies, gingival hyperplasia, and restricted joints appear in infancy.

HGPRT.clue: Purine-salvage enzyme lost in the X-linked syndrome of self-mutilation and gout
HGPRT.rationale: Hypoxanthine and guanine cannot be recycled, so uric acid rises. Allopurinol lowers urate but does not fix the neurologic disease.

WILMS.clue: Childhood kidney tumor of the WT1 gene that does not cross the midline
WILMS.rationale: Aniridia, genitourinary malformations, and hemihypertrophy are associated. Hypertension and hematuria are clinical clues.

PATAU.clue: Trisomy 13 with holoprosencephaly, cleft lip, polydactyly, and cutis aplasia
PATAU.rationale: Rock-bottom feet belong more to trisomy 18. Survival beyond infancy is uncommon.

PRION.clue: Misfolded protein that templates more misfolding and leaves spongiform brain tissue
PRION.rationale: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease causes rapidly progressive dementia and startle myoclonus. Standard sterilization does not reliably destroy the agent.

NEGRI.clue: Eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions of rabies in hippocampal and cerebellar neurons
NEGRI.rationale: The virus travels retrograde along axons. Once hydrophobia and spasms begin, the disease is almost always fatal.

GUMMA.clue: Soft granuloma of tertiary syphilis in skin, bone, or liver
GUMMA.rationale: It is not highly infectious. Aortitis and tabes dorsalis are the other tertiary patterns.

TABES.clue: Dorsal-column degeneration of tertiary syphilis with ataxia and lightning pains
TABES.rationale: Argyll Robertson pupils accommodate but do not react to light. Charcot joints follow loss of position sense.

AVIUM.clue: Mycobacterium of disseminated disease when the CD4 count falls below 50
AVIUM.rationale: Azithromycin prevents it at that threshold. Older adults with structural lung disease can get a more limited pulmonary form.

MUCOR.clue: Broad nonseptate hyphae at right angles that invade vessels in diabetic ketoacidosis
MUCOR.rationale: A black necrotic palate or nasal turbinate is the bedside clue. Surgery plus amphotericin and reversal of the acidosis are required.

TINEA.clue: Dermatophyte infection of keratin that shows branching septate hyphae on potassium hydroxide prep
TINEA.rationale: Capitis in children needs an oral agent because topicals do not reach the hair shaft. Corporis, cruris, and pedis are the other patterns.

EBOLA.clue: Filovirus hemorrhagic fever transmitted by body fluids, with a fruit-bat reservoir
EBOLA.rationale: Care is supportive and barrier precautions are essential. It is distinct from the flavivirus hemorrhagic fevers.

POLIO.clue: Picornavirus that destroys anterior horn cells and causes asymmetric flaccid paralysis without sensory loss
POLIO.rationale: The killed vaccine induces circulating antibody. The oral vaccine also induces gut immunity but can rarely revert.

MUMPS.clue: Paramyxovirus parotitis that can inflame testes, meninges, and the pancreas
MUMPS.rationale: Postpubertal orchitis can impair fertility if bilateral. The virus is a classic cause of aseptic meningitis.

CREST.clue: Limited systemic sclerosis with centromere antibodies, calcinosis, and esophageal dysmotility
CREST.rationale: Raynaud phenomenon, sclerodactyly, and telangiectasias complete the name. Pulmonary hypertension is the serious visceral risk.

PAGET.clue: Phases of lytic then sclerotic bone with a mosaic cement-line pattern and an isolated high alkaline phosphatase
PAGET.rationale: Calcium and phosphate stay normal. High-output heart failure, hearing loss, and later osteosarcoma are complications.

EWING.clue: Diaphyseal small round blue-cell tumor of children with an 11;22 translocation and onion-skin periosteum
EWING.rationale: Glycogen makes the cells PAS positive. It can mimic osteomyelitis clinically.

RENIN.clue: Juxtaglomerular enzyme released when afferent pressure or distal sodium chloride falls
RENIN.rationale: It cleaves angiotensinogen. Beta-1 blockade and high sodium at the macula densa suppress it.

CAPUT.clue: Portal-hypertension veins radiating from the umbilicus
CAPUT.rationale: They reflect recanalized umbilical flow. Esophageal varices and splenomegaly share the same pressure problem.

LYNCH.clue: Mismatch-repair loss with right-sided colon cancer, endometrial cancer, and microsatellite instability
LYNCH.rationale: MSH2 and MLH1 are the common genes. The polyps are few, unlike familial adenomatous polyposis.

HUMPS.clue: Subepithelial immune deposits of poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
HUMPS.rationale: Immunofluorescence is granular, and C3 is low. The latency is weeks after pharyngitis, not days.

BENCE.clue: Urinary light chains of plasma-cell myeloma that a routine dipstick can miss
BENCE.rationale: Urine protein electrophoresis or immunofixation finds them. They injure tubules as cast nephropathy.

MUDDY.clue: Brown granular casts of acute tubular necrosis
MUDDY.rationale: Ischemia or toxins such as aminoglycosides, contrast, and myoglobin are causes. The sediment is dirty rather than filled with cells.

FELTY.clue: Long-standing rheumatoid arthritis with splenomegaly and neutropenia
FELTY.rationale: Leg ulcers and infections follow the low neutrophil count. It is not a separate joint disease.

ROSEA.clue: Herald patch followed by a Christmas-tree trunk rash that resolves on its own
ROSEA.rationale: It affects adolescents and young adults. Secondary syphilis is the important look-alike when palms and soles are involved.

ACTIN.clue: Thin filament that myosin pulls during contraction and that some bacterial toxins ADP-ribosylate
ACTIN.rationale: Clostridioides difficile toxin B depolymerizes it. Cytochalasins also block its polymerization.

TITIN.clue: Giant sarcomere protein that anchors myosin and provides passive elasticity
TITIN.rationale: It spans half the sarcomere. Mutations can cause dilated cardiomyopathy and some muscular dystrophies.

SHUNT.clue: Perfusion without ventilation that does not fully correct when the patient breathes pure oxygen
SHUNT.rationale: ARDS and right-to-left cardiac lesions are examples. The alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient is increased.

BERRY.clue: Saccular outpouching at a circle-of-Willis branch point whose rupture causes the worst headache of life
BERRY.rationale: Anterior communicating and posterior communicating arteries are typical sites. Polycystic kidney disease and Ehlers-Danlos raise the risk.

MEIGS.clue: Ovarian fibroma with ascites and a pleural effusion that resolve when the benign tumor is removed
MEIGS.rationale: CA-125 can be elevated and mimic carcinoma. The syndrome is a diagnosis after the effusion disappears postoperatively.

GOWER.clue: Using the hands to walk up the thighs when standing, a sign of proximal weakness
GOWER.rationale: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is the classic setting. Calf pseudohypertrophy and a high creatine kinase accompany it.

LEBER.clue: Mitochondrial optic neuropathy with painless vision loss in young adults, often men
LEBER.rationale: Maternal inheritance is the pedigree clue. It is not the same disorder as congenital amaurosis.

BROCA.clue: Nonfluent aphasia with preserved comprehension from a dominant inferior frontal lesion
BROCA.rationale: Nearby motor cortex often adds right face and arm weakness. Repetition is impaired.

CROHN.clue: Transmural skip lesions from mouth to anus with noncaseating granulomas and fistulas
CROHN.rationale: The terminal ileum is typical, so B12 deficiency and oxalate kidney stones occur. Smoking worsens it, and anti-TNF drugs are a mainstay.

ILEUM.clue: Bowel segment that absorbs the B12-intrinsic factor complex and reclaims bile salts
ILEUM.rationale: Crohn disease and resection here cause megaloblastic anemia and fat-soluble vitamin loss. Bile-acid diarrhea can follow.

FOAMY.clue: Lipid-laden macrophages of Niemann-Pick disease after sphingomyelinase fails
FOAMY.rationale: Hepatosplenomegaly and neurodegeneration occur in the infantile form. A cherry-red macula can be seen, as in Tay-Sachs.

LISCH.clue: Pigmented iris hamartomas that support neurofibromatosis type 1
LISCH.rationale: Cafe-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, and optic gliomas are the other clues. The gene product normally restrains RAS.

LUPUS.clue: Multisystem disease with anti-Smith and anti-double-stranded-DNA antibodies and low complement
LUPUS.rationale: Immune-complex injury hits kidneys, serosa, and joints. Drug-induced lupus, by contrast, has antihistone antibodies and spares the kidney.

ROCKY.clue: Tick-borne rickettsial vasculitis whose rash starts on wrists and ankles and then involves palms and soles
ROCKY.rationale: The organism invades endothelium. Doxycycline is indicated even in children, and the disease is most common in the south-central United States.

WEISS.clue: Mucosal tear at the gastroesophageal junction after retching, with hematemesis but no transmural hole
WEISS.rationale: Alcohol use and bulimia are settings. A full-thickness rupture into the pleura is a different, surgical emergency.

DANDY.clue: Cystic fourth ventricle, absent cerebellar vermis, and hydrocephalus
DANDY.rationale: It presents in infancy with a large posterior fossa. It is distinct from Chiari malformations.

HAIRY.clue: Indolent B-cell leukemia with a fried-egg appearance and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase
HAIRY.rationale: Massive splenomegaly and pancytopenia occur, and lymph nodes are usually spared. Cladribine is a classic therapy.

MARFAN.clue: Fibrillin defect with upward lens dislocation, aortic root aneurysm, and long fingers
MARFAN.rationale: TGF-beta signaling is excessive. Spontaneous pneumothorax and mitral-valve prolapse are part of the same connective-tissue failure.

WILSON.clue: ATP7B disease with low ceruloplasmin, Kayser-Fleischer rings, and basal-ganglia injury
WILSON.rationale: Copper cannot enter bile or ceruloplasmin. Liver failure, psychiatric change, and hemolysis follow, and penicillamine or trientine chelates the metal.

HURLER.clue: Alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency with corneal clouding, gargoyle facies, and airway obstruction
HURLER.rationale: Heparan and dermatan sulfate accumulate. It is autosomal recessive, unlike the related enzyme defect that spares the cornea.

HUNTER.clue: Iduronate-sulfatase deficiency that is X-linked and lacks corneal clouding
HUNTER.rationale: Behavior is aggressive, and the same two glycosaminoglycans accumulate as in Hurler disease. Enzyme replacement or transplant is used.

KRABBE.clue: Galactocerebrosidase deficiency with globoid cells, optic atrophy, and peripheral neuropathy
KRABBE.rationale: Psychosine kills oligodendrocytes. Infants become irritable and lose milestones.

GIERKE.clue: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency with severe fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, and gout
GIERKE.rationale: The liver cannot release free glucose or complete gluconeogenesis. Hepatomegaly, hyperlipidemia, and doll-like facies are classic.

MENKES.clue: ATP7A defect with kinky hair, hypotonia, and low copper
MENKES.rationale: Copper cannot leave enterocytes, so lysyl oxidase fails and collagen is weak. It is the absorption-side opposite of Wilson disease.

ALPORT.clue: Type IV collagen mutation with hematuria, hearing loss, and eye disease
ALPORT.rationale: The usual inheritance is X-linked. The glomerular basement membrane splits on electron microscopy.

TURNER.clue: 45,X pattern of streak ovaries, coarctation, horseshoe kidney, and cystic hygroma
TURNER.rationale: There is no Barr body. Short stature, webbed neck, and lymphedema complete the picture, and fertility is usually absent.

OROTIC.clue: UMP-synthase deficiency with urinary crystals of a pyrimidine intermediate and megaloblastic anemia not fixed by folate or B12
OROTIC.rationale: There is no hyperammonemia, which separates it from ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency. Uridine treats it by feedback on carbamoyl phosphate.

MECKEL.clue: Persistent vitelline duct with ectopic gastric mucosa and painless bleeding in a child
MECKEL.rationale: The rule of twos describes length, location, and age. A technetium scan finds the gastric mucosa.

CELIAC.clue: Gluten enteropathy with duodenal villous atrophy and tissue-transglutaminase antibodies
CELIAC.rationale: Dermatitis herpetiformis is the skin form. HLA-DQ2 or DQ8 is required, and T-cell lymphoma is a late risk.

SIGNET.clue: Diffuse gastric carcinoma cells whose mucin pushes the nucleus aside
SIGNET.rationale: E-cadherin loss lets cells infiltrate as linitis plastica. Ovarian metastases of this pattern are Krukenberg tumors.

SODIUM.clue: Cation whose serum fall must be corrected slowly to avoid osmotic demyelination
SODIUM.rationale: The brain has adapted to hypotonicity by losing osmolytes. A rise faster than about 8 to 10 mEq in a day can injure the pons.

TETANY.clue: Muscle spasm of low ionized calcium, unmasked by Chvostek and Trousseau signs
TETANY.rationale: Respiratory alkalosis can trigger it by binding calcium to albumin. Hypoparathyroidism and vitamin D deficiency are sustained causes.

PORTAL.clue: Venous system whose hypertension produces varices, splenomegaly, and ascites
PORTAL.rationale: Cirrhosis is the usual cause. A beta blocker or band ligation prevents first variceal bleeding.

RABIES.clue: Bullet-shaped virus that reaches the brain by retrograde axonal transport
RABIES.rationale: Bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes are reservoirs. After exposure, vaccine plus immunoglobulin infiltrated at the wound is preventive; symptoms mean the disease is fatal.

STATUS.clue: Seizure activity that does not stop, treated first with a benzodiazepine
STATUS.rationale: Lorazepam or diazepam is immediate, then a longer-acting agent such as phenytoin, valproate, or levetiracetam. Ongoing activity injures neurons.

ANEMIA.clue: Low red-cell mass whose microcytic, macrocytic, or hemolytic pattern narrows the cause
ANEMIA.rationale: Iron deficiency lowers ferritin and raises transferrin. B12 deficiency adds dorsal-column injury that folate deficiency does not.

TARGET.clue: Erythrocyte with a bull's-eye of hemoglobin, seen in thalassemia, hemoglobin C, and asplenia
TARGET.rationale: Extra membrane relative to hemoglobin creates the shape. Liver disease can produce the same film.

SMUDGE.clue: Fragile lymphocytes crushed on the film in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
SMUDGE.rationale: The disease is a CD5-positive B-cell neoplasm of older adults. Hypogammaglobulinemia and autoimmune hemolysis are complications.

LANCET.clue: Gram-positive diplococcus shape of the organism that is optochin sensitive and bile soluble
LANCET.rationale: It is the common cause of lobar pneumonia, otitis, sinusitis, and adult meningitis. A capsule is the virulence factor, and asplenia is a major risk.

MORULA.clue: Mulberry inclusion of anaplasma or ehrlichia inside white cells
MORULA.rationale: Ixodes ticks carry anaplasma inside granulocytes, and the lone-star tick carries ehrlichia inside monocytes. Doxycycline treats both.

CHAGAS.clue: Trypanosoma cruzi disease with dilated cardiomyopathy, megaesophagus, and megacolon
CHAGAS.rationale: The reduviid bug transmits it in Latin America. Romana sign is unilateral periorbital swelling at the entry site.

TAENIA.clue: Tapeworm whose eggs, if swallowed, seed the brain and cause seizures
TAENIA.rationale: That cysticercosis route is the pork species. Eating cyst-containing meat causes intestinal tapeworm instead.

CEREUS.clue: Spore-forming rod of reheated rice that causes vomiting from a preformed toxin
CEREUS.rationale: A separate heat-labile toxin causes a later diarrheal illness. The spores survive boiling.

TETANI.clue: Toxin that cleaves SNARE proteins in inhibitory interneurons and produces lockjaw
TETANI.rationale: Glycine and GABA release fails, so muscles spasm. The toxoid vaccine prevents disease; immunoglobulin neutralizes unbound toxin.

UREASE.clue: Enzyme that lets gastric spiral bacteria buffer acid, detected by a breath test
UREASE.rationale: The same activity in Proteus generates struvite stones. Eradication of the gastric organism lowers ulcer and MALT-lymphoma risk.

PLAGUE.clue: Yersinia infection of fleas and rodents with buboes and bipolar safety-pin staining
PLAGUE.rationale: Pneumonic form spreads person to person. Streptomycin or gentamicin is traditional therapy.

TYPHUS.clue: Louse-borne rickettsial fever whose rash starts on the trunk and spares the palms
TYPHUS.rationale: Epidemic disease is Rickettsia prowazekii. It spreads outward, the opposite direction of Rocky Mountain spotted fever.

CULLEN.rationale: Retroperitoneal blood tracks to the abdominal wall. Flank ecchymosis is the companion sign.

BEHCET.clue: Oral and genital ulcers with uveitis and a pathergy test, along the Silk Road
BEHCET.rationale: It can inflame vessels of any size and cause thrombosis. HLA-B51 is associated.

HENOCH.clue: IgA vasculitis of children with palpable purpura, arthralgia, and abdominal pain
HENOCH.rationale: Renal involvement is an IgA nephropathy. It often follows an upper-respiratory infection.

NIACIN.clue: Vitamin B3 used for NAD, whose deficiency is pellagra and whose drug use causes prostaglandin flushing
NIACIN.rationale: Carcinoid and isoniazid can deplete it. Hartnup disease wastes tryptophan, the precursor.

BIOTIN.clue: Vitamin required by carboxylases and depleted by raw egg-white avidin
BIOTIN.rationale: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase and pyruvate carboxylase need it. Deficiency causes dermatitis, alopecia, and acidosis.

FOLATE.clue: One-carbon vitamin whose deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia without neuropathy
FOLATE.rationale: Neural-tube closure needs it before conception. Methotrexate, trimethoprim, and phenytoin interfere with its pathway.

MALATE.clue: Shuttle metabolite that carries reducing equivalents from cytosol into mitochondria
MALATE.rationale: The malate-aspartate shuttle feeds NADH to the electron-transport chain. Cytosolic NADH from glycolysis cannot cross the inner membrane directly.

LEPTIN.clue: Adipocyte hormone that signals satiety at the hypothalamus
LEPTIN.rationale: Deficiency or receptor defects cause rare obesity with hyperphagia. Ordinary obesity usually has high levels and resistance.

PEPSIN.clue: Chief-cell protease secreted as a zymogen and activated by gastric acid
PEPSIN.rationale: It starts protein digestion. It is not the pancreatic enzyme activated by enterokinase.

LIPASE.clue: Pancreatic enzyme more specific than amylase for acute pancreatitis
LIPASE.rationale: It stays elevated longer. Hypertriglyceridemia, gallstones, and alcohol are leading causes of the illness.

DYNEIN.clue: Motor that walks cargo and cilia toward the minus end of microtubules
DYNEIN.rationale: A defective arm causes immotile cilia, sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and situs inversus. Kinesin walks the other direction.

LIGASE.clue: Enzyme that seals nicks in the DNA backbone during replication and repair
LIGASE.rationale: It joins Okazaki fragments. Defects contribute to some radiation-sensitivity syndromes.

GYRASE.clue: Bacterial type II topoisomerase blocked by fluoroquinolones
GYRASE.rationale: It introduces negative supercoils so the chromosome can unwind. Eukaryotic topoisomerase II is a different drug target.

SCURVY.clue: Vitamin C deficiency with bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhage, and poor wound healing
SCURVY.rationale: Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases cannot stabilize collagen without ascorbate. Corkscrew hairs are a bedside clue.

ANERGY.clue: T-cell unresponsiveness when antigen is seen without a costimulatory second signal
ANERGY.rationale: The same word describes failure of delayed-type skin tests. Either way, the lymphocyte does not respond.

THYMUS.clue: Organ of positive and negative T-cell selection, absent in DiGeorge syndrome
THYMUS.rationale: Hassall corpuscles mark the medulla. The third pharyngeal pouch also supplies the inferior parathyroids.

GRAVES.clue: TSH-receptor-stimulating antibodies with diffuse uptake, ophthalmopathy, and pretibial myxedema
GRAVES.rationale: The eye disease is fibroblast and glycosaminoglycan driven and may not track the hormone level. Methimazole, radioiodine, or surgery treats the gland.

LIDDLE.clue: Gain-of-function sodium channel with hypertension, low aldosterone, and low renin
LIDDLE.rationale: It mimics hyperaldosteronism but the hormone is suppressed. Amiloride blocks the overactive channel.

HORNER.clue: Ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis from interrupted sympathetic supply to the eye
HORNER.rationale: A Pancoast tumor, carotid dissection, and lateral medullary stroke are causes. Anhidrosis depends on which neuron is hit.

ARGYLL.clue: Pupil that accommodates but does not react, classically in neurosyphilis
ARGYLL.rationale: The midbrain light reflex is interrupted while the near pathway is spared. Diabetic neuropathy can mimic it.

AUREUS.clue: Coagulase-positive gram-positive coccus that binds IgG backward with protein A
AUREUS.rationale: It causes abscesses, acute endocarditis, and toxic shock. The superantigen toxin cross-links MHC II and the T-cell receptor outside the groove.

STATIN.clue: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that lowers LDL and stabilizes plaque
STATIN.rationale: Myopathy rises when CYP3A4 inhibitors or fibrates are added. The drugs are teratogenic and can inflame the liver.

KETONE.clue: Fuel made in liver mitochondria from fatty acids when insulin is low
KETONE.rationale: Acetone causes the fruity breath of ketoacidosis. The nitroprusside test detects acetoacetate better than beta-hydroxybutyrate.

MYOSIN.clue: Thick filament ATPase that forms the cross-bridge
MYOSIN.rationale: Calcium binding to troponin C exposes the actin site. Beta-myosin heavy-chain mutations cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

MANTLE.clue: Lymphoma of cyclin D1 overexpression from t(11;14), CD5 positive like CLL
MANTLE.rationale: It arises from the mantle zone around follicles. The course is usually more aggressive than follicular lymphoma.

KAPOSI.clue: HHV-8 spindle-cell vascular tumor of advanced HIV, with slit-like spaces
KAPOSI.rationale: Classic Mediterranean disease in older men is a separate, indolent form. Treating the underlying HIV often shrinks the lesions.

DENGUE.clue: Aedes-borne flavivirus of breakbone fever that can cause shock on a second infection
DENGUE.rationale: Antibody-dependent enhancement is the proposed mechanism of severe disease. Platelets fall and plasma leaks.

HERPES.clue: Family of enveloped double-stranded DNA viruses that establish lifelong latency
HERPES.rationale: HSV, VZV, EBV, and CMV are the high-yield members. Acyclovir needs a viral kinase that CMV does not rely on in the same way.

LIBMAN.clue: Sterile vegetations on both sides of a valve leaflet in lupus
LIBMAN.rationale: They are not infective. Antiphospholipid antibodies raise the embolic risk.

FIBRATE.clue: PPAR-alpha agonist that lowers triglycerides and can cause gallstones
FIBRATE.rationale: It induces lipoprotein lipase. Combined with a statin, especially gemfibrozil, the myopathy risk climbs.

ACETONE.clue: Volatile ketone responsible for the fruity breath of ketoacidosis
ACETONE.rationale: It is not an acid and does not drive the anion gap. Acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate do.

GLYCINE.clue: Inhibitory spinal transmitter that tetanus toxin prevents from being released
GLYCINE.rationale: It is also a heme precursor and is conjugated to bile acids. Nonketotic hyperglycinemia is a rare seizure disorder of infants.

PROLINE.clue: Imino acid abundant in collagen and hydroxylated with the help of vitamin C
PROLINE.rationale: Hydroxyproline stabilizes the triple helix. Scurvy fails that step and vessels become fragile.

HISTONE.clue: Protein octamer that DNA wraps, and whose acetylation loosens chromatin
HISTONE.rationale: Acetylation favors transcription. Deacetylase inhibitors are used in some T-cell lymphomas.

PRIMASE.clue: Enzyme that lays down the RNA primer DNA polymerase needs
PRIMASE.rationale: DNA polymerases can only extend a strand. The primer is later removed and the gap filled.

ATROPHY.clue: Shrinkage of an organ from disuse, denervation, loss of hormone, or reduced blood supply
ATROPHY.rationale: The cell number or cell size falls. It is reversible early, unlike the point of no return in necrosis.

ADENOMA.clue: Benign glandular tumor that can secrete hormone or become a carcinoma
ADENOMA.rationale: Colonic, pituitary, parathyroid, and hepatic examples behave differently. A hepatic one is linked to oral contraceptives and can rupture.

SARCOMA.clue: Malignant mesenchymal tumor that usually spreads in blood rather than lymph
SARCOMA.rationale: Osteosarcoma, liposarcoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma are examples. Hematogenous lung metastases are typical.

AMYLOID.clue: Misfolded protein that stains Congo red and glows apple green under polarized light
AMYLOID.rationale: AL comes from light chains, AA from chronic inflammation, and ATTR from transthyretin. The kidney and heart are frequent targets.

CASEOUS.clue: Cheese-like necrosis inside granulomas of secondary tuberculosis
CASEOUS.rationale: It is a mix of coagulative and liquefactive patterns. Noncaseating granulomas suggest sarcoidosis or Crohn disease instead.

HODGKIN.clue: Lymphoma with Reed-Sternberg cells, contiguous node spread, and often a good response to therapy
HODGKIN.rationale: The malignant cell is a crippled B cell that is CD15 and CD30 positive. Nodular-sclerosis type brings collagen bands and lacunar cells.

BURKITT.clue: Starry-sky lymphoma of c-myc translocation, EBV, and a very high proliferation rate
BURKITT.rationale: Endemic disease presents in the jaw. Sporadic disease often presents as an ileocecal mass.

MYELOMA.clue: Plasma-cell cancer with CRAB findings: calcium, renal failure, anemia, and bone lesions
MYELOMA.rationale: Clock-face chromatin and rouleaux are smear clues. Light chains, not just albumin, must be sought in the urine.

VIRCHOW.clue: Triad of stasis, endothelial injury, and hypercoagulability that explains thrombosis
VIRCHOW.rationale: The same eponym also names a left supraclavicular node seeded by abdominal, especially gastric, cancer.

LINITIS.clue: Leather-bottle stomach of diffuse signet-ring gastric carcinoma
LINITIS.rationale: The wall is thickened and stiff rather than mass-forming. Prognosis is poor because the tumor infiltrates early.

BARRETT.clue: Intestinal metaplasia of the distal esophagus after chronic reflux, with goblet cells
BARRETT.rationale: It is the precursor of esophageal adenocarcinoma. Squamous carcinoma of the esophagus is the smoking and alcohol disease instead.

WHIPPLE.clue: PAS-positive macrophages packing the lamina propria after infection by Tropheryma
WHIPPLE.rationale: Malabsorption, arthritis, and neurologic or cardiac disease occur together. It is not a celiac mimic that responds to gluten withdrawal.

PYLORIC.clue: Infantile gastric-outlet obstruction with an olive mass and hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis
PYLORIC.rationale: Vomiting is projectile and nonbilious, usually in the first weeks of life. Erythromycin exposure is a risk factor.

ANNULAR.clue: Ring of pancreatic tissue around the duodenum that can obstruct it
ANNULAR.rationale: The presentation is bilious vomiting. It is a rotation and fusion anomaly, not an atresia.

BILIOUS.clue: Green vomitus that means the obstruction is distal to the ampulla of Vater
BILIOUS.rationale: Duodenal atresia, malrotation with volvulus, and annular pancreas are causes. Nonbilious vomiting points above the ampulla, as in pyloric stenosis.

CURRANT.clue: Jelly stool of intussusception in a toddler
CURRANT.rationale: A lead point such as a Meckel diverticulum or lymphoid hyperplasia may start it. Air or contrast enema can be both diagnostic and therapeutic.

NODOSUM.clue: Tender pretibial panniculitis associated with strep, sarcoid, inflammatory bowel disease, and endemic fungi
NODOSUM.rationale: The nodules do not ulcerate. It is a reactive septal process, not a vasculitis that needs immediate immunosuppression in every case.

BUERGER.clue: Segmental thrombosing vasculitis of smokers that can autoamputate digits
BUERGER.rationale: Superficial thrombophlebitis and claudication occur. The only effective treatment is to stop tobacco completely.

RAYNAUD.clue: Cold-induced white-blue-red color change of digits from vasospasm
RAYNAUD.rationale: Connective-tissue disease is suspected when it is severe or unilateral-sparing and begins later in life. Calcium-channel blockers relax the spasm.

WEGENER.clue: c-ANCA vasculitis of upper airway, lung, and kidney, now called granulomatosis with polyangiitis
WEGENER.rationale: The antigen is proteinase 3. Nodules cavitate, and the glomerulonephritis is pauci-immune.

BABESIA.clue: Intraerythrocyte parasite that forms a Maltese cross and causes severe hemolysis after splenectomy
BABESIA.rationale: Ixodes is the tick, so Lyme coinfection occurs. Atovaquone plus azithromycin is usual treatment.

CHOLERA.clue: Toxin that ADP-ribosylates Gs, locks adenylate cyclase on, and causes rice-water stool
CHOLERA.rationale: The mucosa is not invaded, so fecal leukocytes are absent. Oral rehydration replaces the bicarbonate-rich fluid.

HYDATID.clue: Sheep-dog tapeworm cyst in the liver that can cause anaphylaxis if it ruptures
HYDATID.rationale: Echinococcus is the organism. Surgery or aspiration is done carefully, with albendazole cover.

ASCARIS.clue: Large roundworm that migrates through the lung and can obstruct the intestine
ASCARIS.rationale: Eggs must mature in soil before they are infectious. A bolus of worms is a cause of bowel obstruction and biliary colic.

SCABIES.clue: Mite that burrows in finger webs and causes pruritus worse at night
SCABIES.rationale: Permethrin treats ordinary infestation, and close contacts are treated too. Crusted disease in immunosuppression may need ivermectin.

VARICES.clue: Dilated submucosal esophageal veins of portal hypertension that can bleed massively
VARICES.rationale: Octreotide and band ligation are acute measures. A nonselective beta blocker is used for prevention.

ASCITES.clue: Peritoneal fluid of portal hypertension that can become infected without a surgical abdomen
ASCITES.rationale: A neutrophil count above 250 in the fluid diagnoses spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. Third-generation cephalosporins cover the usual gram-negative rods.

CHANCRE.clue: Painless genital ulcer of primary syphilis
CHANCRE.rationale: The organism is too thin to see on Gram stain and is found on darkfield microscopy. A painful ulcer suggests chancroid instead.

LEPROSY.clue: Mycobacterium that cannot be cultured on artificial media and prefers cool skin
LEPROSY.rationale: Tuberculoid disease is Th1 and paucibacillary. Lepromatous disease is Th2, with leonine facies and a negative lepromin test.

MILIARY.rationale: Innumerable small nodules appear in lung, liver, and marrow. It is a form of progressive primary or reactivated disease.

GIARDIA.clue: Flagellate that causes foul fatty diarrhea after camping and in IgA deficiency
GIARDIA.rationale: It does not invade, so the stool is not bloody. Trophozoites attach in the duodenum and metronidazole is the usual drug.

MALTESE.clue: Cross formed by Babesia inside a red cell
MALTESE.rationale: The same tick transmits Lyme disease. Severe disease strikes people without a spleen.

MEASLES.clue: Paramyxovirus with cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and Koplik spots before a descending rash
MEASLES.rationale: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis can appear years later. Vitamin A lowers morbidity in deficiency.

RUBELLA.clue: Togavirus whose congenital form causes cataracts, deafness, and a patent ductus
RUBELLA.rationale: The postnatal rash is milder than measles and lymphadenopathy is postauricular. The vaccine is live and contraindicated in pregnancy.

ROSEOLA.clue: HHV-6 illness of high fever that defervesces as a trunk rash appears
ROSEOLA.rationale: Febrile seizures are the main acute risk. It is the sixth childhood exanthem.

MARBURG.clue: Filovirus cousin of Ebola that also causes hemorrhagic fever
MARBURG.rationale: Fruit bats are the reservoir. Management is supportive and isolation is strict.

EPSTEIN.clue: Surname linked to the herpesvirus of mononucleosis, Burkitt lymphoma, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma
EPSTEIN.rationale: The virus immortalizes B cells through CD21. A heterophile antibody is the classic screening test.

QUININE.clue: Cinchona alkaloid used for malaria that causes tinnitus, headache, and visual change
QUININE.rationale: That symptom cluster is cinchonism. It can also trigger hemolysis in G6PD deficiency and hypoglycemia by releasing insulin.

DIGOXIN.clue: Cardiac glycoside that inhibits the sodium-potassium pump and increases vagal tone
DIGOXIN.rationale: Intracellular calcium rises, so contractility increases. Hypokalemia promotes toxicity, which includes yellow vision and atrial tachycardia with block.

ANTHRAX.clue: Spore-forming rod with a polyglutamate capsule, a black eschar, and a widened mediastinum
ANTHRAX.rationale: Edema factor is an adenylate cyclase and lethal factor cuts MAP kinase. The pulmonary form comes from spores, not person-to-person spread.

SJOGREN.clue: Lymphocytic destruction of salivary and lacrimal glands with anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies
SJOGREN.rationale: Dental caries and corneal injury follow the dryness. B-cell lymphoma risk is increased, and anti-Ro can cause neonatal heart block.

JEJUNUM.clue: Small-bowel segment that absorbs most folate, just distal to the iron-absorbing duodenum
JEJUNUM.rationale: Celiac disease hits the duodenum and proximal bowel hardest. Tropical sprue involves a longer stretch and responds to antibiotics and folate.

JARISCH.clue: Fever and hypotension hours after antibiotics kill spirochetes, from a cytokine surge
JARISCH.rationale: It is not a penicillin allergy. Syphilis and Lyme treatment are the classic settings, and the drug is not stopped for this reaction alone.

GAUCHER.clue: Most common lysosomal storage disease, with crumpled-paper macrophages and bone crises
GAUCHER.rationale: Glucocerebrosidase is deficient and glucocerebroside accumulates. Avascular necrosis of the femur and hepatosplenomegaly are typical of type 1.

MCARDLE.clue: Muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency with exercise cramps and a flat venous lactate curve
MCARDLE.rationale: A second wind can appear as blood-borne fuel arrives. Myoglobinuria may follow a hard bout of exercise.

STEROID.clue: Drug class that inhibits NF-kB, causes neutrophilia by demargination, and suppresses fever
STEROID.rationale: Long use thins bone, raises glucose, and suppresses the adrenal axis. Stop gradually after prolonged therapy.

INSULIN.clue: Tyrosine-kinase hormone that moves GLUT4 to muscle and fat membrane and drives potassium inward
INSULIN.rationale: It does not gate glucose entry into the liver, brain, or red cells. Deficiency allows lipolysis and ketoacidosis.

TRYPSIN.clue: Pancreatic protease activated in the gut by enterokinase, which then activates the other zymogens
TRYPSIN.rationale: Premature activation inside the pancreas starts autodigestion. It is the key that turns on the enzyme cascade.

AMYLASE.clue: Starch-splitting enzyme that rises in pancreatitis but also in salivary disease and bowel perforation
AMYLASE.rationale: Lipase is more specific for the pancreas. Levels do not predict severity.

LACTASE.clue: Brush-border enzyme whose loss after infection or with age causes osmotic diarrhea and gas
LACTASE.rationale: Undigested lactose is fermented by colonic bacteria. Stool osmotic gap is high and the diarrhea stops when milk stops.

SUCRASE.clue: Brush-border enzyme whose congenital deficiency causes diarrhea when sucrose is introduced
SUCRASE.rationale: Glucose remains tolerable because the sodium-glucose transporter is intact. The diarrhea is osmotic.

ALBUMIN.clue: Plasma protein that sets oncotic pressure and carries unconjugated bilirubin, calcium, and many drugs
ALBUMIN.rationale: Low levels from liver failure or nephrotic syndrome cause edema. Corrected calcium rises when this carrier is low.

PLASMIN.clue: Fibrin-cleaving enzyme generated by tissue plasminogen activator
PLASMIN.rationale: Alpha-2 antiplasmin and PAI-1 restrain it. Unchecked activity, as in thrombolysis, raises bleeding risk.

KERATIN.clue: Intermediate filament of epithelium and the pearl-forming protein of squamous cancers
KERATIN.rationale: Anti-cytokeratin stains mark carcinomas. Molluscum and HPV lesions are epithelial but not defined by keratin pearls.

ELASTIN.clue: Stretch protein destroyed in emphysema when alpha-1 antitrypsin is missing or overwhelmed
ELASTIN.rationale: Smoking brings neutrophils and their protease. Panacinar basal emphysema is the inherited pattern.

CALCIUM.clue: Divalent cation of bone, coagulation, and muscle, low in the saponification of pancreatitis
CALCIUM.rationale: Albumin binds part of the measured total. Tetany, prolonged QT, and Chvostek sign mark the ionized deficit.

GASTRIN.clue: Antral hormone that raises acid through ECL histamine and directly on parietal cells
GASTRIN.rationale: A gastrinoma causes ulcers beyond the bulb and diarrhea. High gastrin with low pH separates it from ordinary achlorhydria.

MOTILIN.clue: Hormone of the migrating motor complex that erythromycin can mimic
MOTILIN.rationale: It sweeps the fasting gut. Macrolide agonism explains both prokinetic use and some of the cramping.

GHRELIN.clue: Stomach hormone that stimulates appetite and growth-hormone release
GHRELIN.rationale: Levels rise before meals and in fasting, and fall after bypass surgery. It opposes leptin at the hypothalamus.

RETINOL.clue: Vitamin A alcohol needed for night vision and epithelial differentiation
RETINOL.rationale: Deficiency causes night blindness and squamous metaplasia. Excess and the acne retinoids are teratogenic.

RICKETS.clue: Childhood failure of growth-plate mineralization from vitamin D deficiency
RICKETS.rationale: Rachitic rosary, bowed legs, and craniotabes are findings. Adults with the same deficit get osteomalacia instead.

CITRATE.clue: TCA intermediate that also signals the cell has enough energy by inhibiting phosphofructokinase-1
CITRATE.rationale: It is the product of acetyl-CoA plus oxaloacetate. In urine it binds calcium and protects against stones.

LACTATE.clue: End product of anaerobic glycolysis that accumulates when mitochondria cannot reoxidize NADH
LACTATE.rationale: Shock, ischemia, and mitochondrial toxins raise it and open an anion gap. The Cori cycle lets the liver remake glucose from it.

ALANINE.clue: Amino acid that ferries amino groups from muscle pyruvate to the liver for gluconeogenesis
ALANINE.rationale: Transamination pairs this carrier with pyruvate. The liver uses the carbon skeleton to remake glucose during a fast.

LEUCINE.clue: Strictly ketogenic branched-chain amino acid accumulated in maple-syrup urine disease
LEUCINE.rationale: The branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase is the deficient enzyme. Thiamine is a cofactor, and the odor is sweet.

ACETATE.clue: Two-carbon product of ethanol metabolism and a building block of acetyl-CoA
ACETATE.rationale: Ethanol oxidation consumes NAD+ and stalls gluconeogenesis, so fasting drinkers become hypoglycemic.

KETONES.clue: Alternative fuels the brain can use in starvation, absent when insulin is present
KETONES.rationale: They appear in diabetic ketoacidosis and in prolonged fasting. Oxaloacetate shortage diverts acetyl-CoA into their synthesis.

ANKYRIN.clue: Red-cell membrane protein mutated, along with spectrin, in hereditary spherocytosis
ANKYRIN.rationale: Vertical interactions fail and membrane is lost. Osmotic fragility, pigment stones, and an aplastic crisis from parvovirus follow.

NEPHRIN.clue: Slit-diaphragm protein whose mutation causes congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type
NEPHRIN.rationale: Massive albuminuria begins in utero. The glomerular filtration barrier fails at the podocyte.

TUBULIN.clue: Microtubule subunit bound by colchicine, vinca alkaloids, and benzimidazoles
TUBULIN.rationale: Polymerization is blocked by those drugs. Taxanes do the opposite and stabilize the polymer.

KINESIN.clue: Motor that carries cargo toward the plus end of microtubules, away from the cell body
KINESIN.rationale: It is anterograde axonal transport. Dynein is retrograde, which is how rabies and herpes travel toward the soma.

WARFARIN.clue: Oral anticoagulant that blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase and is followed with INR
WARFARIN.rationale: Factor VII falls first, and protein C falls just as fast, so skin necrosis can occur at the start. It is teratogenic and reversed with vitamin K or clotting-factor replacement.

RIFAMPIN.clue: Drug that inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase, turns body fluids orange, and induces many CYP enzymes
RIFAMPIN.rationale: It is used for tuberculosis and meningococcal prophylaxis. Resistance emerges if it is given alone.

CEFEPIME.clue: Fourth-generation cephalosporin with reliable activity against Pseudomonas
CEFEPIME.rationale: It covers many gram-positive and gram-negative organisms but not MRSA or anaerobes well. Neurotoxicity rises if the dose is not reduced in kidney failure.

IMIPENEM.clue: Carbapenem paired with cilastatin so a renal enzyme does not destroy it
IMIPENEM.rationale: The spectrum includes anaerobes and Pseudomonas. Seizures are the dose-limiting risk, especially when GFR is low.

GLARGINE.clue: Long-acting insulin formulation with no pronounced peak and no mixing with other insulins
GLARGINE.rationale: It precipitates at body pH and is absorbed slowly. Nocturnal hypoglycemia is less than with intermediate protamine insulin.

ACARBOSE.clue: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that delays carbohydrate absorption and causes gas
ACARBOSE.rationale: Hypoglycemia on this drug must be treated with glucose, not table sugar, because sucrose cleavage is blocked. It does not cause insulin release.

KUSSMAUL.clue: Neck veins that rise on inspiration, the classic sign of constrictive pericarditis
KUSSMAUL.rationale: The sign reflects a heart that cannot accept the inspiratory rise in venous return. The same eponym is used for the deep, rapid breathing of metabolic acidosis.

MANNITOL.clue: Osmotic diuretic used to lower intracranial pressure, and dangerous in heart failure
MANNITOL.rationale: It is filtered and not reabsorbed, so water stays in the tubule. Pulmonary edema is the reason to avoid it when the heart cannot handle the volume.

LOSARTAN.clue: Angiotensin-receptor blocker that does not raise bradykinin and also lowers uric acid
LOSARTAN.rationale: Cough is uncommon, but hyperkalemia, a rise in creatinine in renal-artery stenosis, and pregnancy risk remain. It blocks AT1 receptors.

ATENOLOL.clue: Renally cleared beta-1 blocker that can hide the tachycardia of hypoglycemia
ATENOLOL.rationale: It enters the brain less than lipophilic beta blockers. Sweating from low glucose can still occur.

ADENOSINE.clue: Very short-acting nucleoside that opens potassium channels at the AV node to stop SVT
ADENOSINE.rationale: The half-life is seconds. Caffeine and theophylline block it, and it can cause bronchospasm and a brief pause.

IMATINIB.clue: Tyrosine-kinase inhibitor of BCR-ABL and of c-KIT
IMATINIB.rationale: It turned chronic myeloid leukemia into a chronic disease and also treats gastrointestinal stromal tumor. Fluid retention is a common effect.

MORPHINE.clue: Full mu agonist that releases histamine and causes miosis, constipation, and respiratory depression
MORPHINE.rationale: Tolerance develops to sedation but not fully to constipation or pinpoint pupils. It can spasm the sphincter of Oddi.

FENTANYL.clue: Potent mu agonist that does not release histamine and is given as patches only to opioid-tolerant patients
FENTANYL.rationale: Chest-wall rigidity can follow a rapid IV dose. Heat on a patch increases absorption.

KETAMINE.clue: NMDA-antagonist anesthetic that raises blood pressure and dilates bronchi
KETAMINE.rationale: Dissociation and emergence reactions are expected. It is useful when hypotension or bronchospasm makes other induction drugs risky.

PROPOFOL.clue: GABA-potentiating anesthetic in a lipid emulsion that drops blood pressure
PROPOFOL.rationale: Prolonged high-dose infusion can cause metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, and bradycardia. The urine may turn green.

LEVODOPA.clue: Dopamine precursor that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is paired with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor
LEVODOPA.rationale: The partner drug reduces nausea and lets more precursor reach the brain. Long-term use brings wearing-off and dyskinesias.

ATROPINE.clue: Muscarinic antagonist used for bradycardia and for the cholinergic toxidrome of organophosphates
ATROPINE.rationale: It dries secretions and dilates pupils but does not reverse nicotinic muscle weakness. An oxime is added to regenerate the enzyme.

COLLAGEN.clue: Triple-helix protein: type I in bone, type II in cartilage, type III in vessels, type IV in basement membrane
COLLAGEN.rationale: Vitamin C is required for hydroxylation. Defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta, Ehlers-Danlos features, and Alport syndrome depending on the chain.

SPECTRIN.clue: Red-cell scaffold protein whose loss, with ankyrin, causes hereditary spherocytosis
SPECTRIN.rationale: Membrane sheds, the MCHC rises, and pigment gallstones form. Splenectomy helps after vaccines against encapsulated organisms.

TROPONIN.clue: Cardiac regulatory protein that is the preferred blood marker of myocardial injury
TROPONIN.rationale: It rises within hours and stays up for days. It is more specific than CK-MB for heart muscle.

GLYCOGEN.clue: Branched glucose store of liver and muscle; muscle cannot release it as free blood glucose
GLYCOGEN.rationale: Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase. Liver glycogen maintains blood glucose during a short fast.

SYPHILIS.clue: Spirochete stages of a painless chancre, a palm-and-sole rash, then aortitis or dorsal-column loss
SYPHILIS.rationale: Nontreponemal tests screen and treponemal tests confirm. Penicillin is the treatment, and a cytokine surge after the first dose is not an allergy.

DIGEORGE.clue: 22q11 failure of the third and fourth pouches, with no thymus, no parathyroids, and conotruncal heart defects
DIGEORGE.rationale: Hypocalcemia and viral or fungal infections follow. The face is often dysmorphic and the thymic shadow is absent.

SQUAMOUS.clue: Central lung cancer with keratin pearls, cavitation, and PTHrP-driven hypercalcemia
SQUAMOUS.rationale: Smoking is the dominant risk. Intercellular bridges on histology separate it from small-cell carcinoma, which is also central.

XANTHOMA.clue: Lipid-laden skin or tendon deposit, Achilles in familial hypercholesterolemia and eruptive when triglycerides are very high
XANTHOMA.rationale: Xanthelasma on the eyelids is the softer cousin. The finding points to a lipoprotein disorder, not a primary skin tumor.

NALOXONE.clue: Short-acting opioid antagonist that reverses respiratory depression and can precipitate withdrawal
NALOXONE.rationale: Repeat doses are often needed because the agonist outlasts it. It does not reverse benzodiazepines.

JAUNDICE.clue: Yellow sclera and skin that appear once bilirubin is high enough to see
JAUNDICE.rationale: The sclera shows it first because elastin binds the pigment. Unconjugated pigment does not darken the urine; the water-soluble fraction does.

FUROSEMIDE.clue: Loop diuretic that blocks the triple cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
FUROSEMIDE.rationale: Calcium and magnesium are lost with sodium, unlike the distal-tubule diuretic that raises serum calcium. Hearing can be injured by a fast IV push, and a contraction alkalosis follows.

VERAPAMIL.clue: Non-dihydropyridine calcium blocker that slows the AV node and often constipates
VERAPAMIL.rationale: It is a negative inotrope and should not be combined with a beta blocker. It raises digoxin levels.

METFORMIN.clue: Biguanide that activates AMPK, lowers hepatic glucose output, and does not cause hypoglycemia alone
METFORMIN.rationale: Lactic acidosis is the rare danger when GFR is low or contrast is given. Long-term use can lower B12.

BOTULINUM.clue: Toxin that cleaves SNARE proteins at the neuromuscular junction and causes descending flaccid paralysis
BOTULINUM.rationale: Acetylcholine release fails, the opposite of the tetanus pattern in inhibitory interneurons. Honey spores cause the infant form; preformed toxin in canned food causes the food-borne form.

MACROLIDE.clue: 50S antibiotic class that also stimulates motilin receptors and can prolong QT
MACROLIDE.rationale: Some members strongly inhibit CYP3A4. The class covers atypical pneumonia and is an alternative in penicillin allergy for strep throat.

ALBUTEROL.clue: Short-acting beta-2 agonist that relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and drives potassium into cells
ALBUTEROL.rationale: Tremor and tachycardia are expected. It is rescue therapy, not the anti-inflammatory treatment of persistent asthma.

AROMATASE.clue: Adipose enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens and is blocked in postmenopausal hormone-positive breast cancer
AROMATASE.rationale: Inhibitors lower estrogen after menopause and speed bone loss. A selective receptor modulator used in the same cancers blocks the breast but can stimulate the endometrium.

BLEOMYCIN.clue: Free-radical anticancer drug that scars the lung and spares the marrow
BLEOMYCIN.rationale: Hydrolase that inactivates it is low in skin and lung, so those tissues are hit. High inspired oxygen adds to the lung injury.

CISPLATIN.clue: Platinum agent that cross-links DNA and is toxic to kidney, ear, and the vomiting center
CISPLATIN.rationale: Chloride diuresis and amifostine limit the renal injury. Magnesium wasting and severe nausea are expected.

VALPROATE.clue: Broad anticonvulsant that is hepatotoxic, teratogenic for the neural tube, and can raise ammonia
VALPROATE.rationale: It inhibits CYP enzymes and causes tremor and weight gain. It is avoided in pregnancy and in young children with mitochondrial disease.

PHENYTOIN.clue: Sodium-channel anticonvulsant with zero-order kinetics, gingival overgrowth, and fetal anomalies
PHENYTOIN.rationale: It induces CYP enzymes and vitamin D metabolism. Stevens-Johnson syndrome and ataxia at high levels are classic.

LIDOCAINE.clue: Class Ib sodium-channel blocker used for ischemic ventricular arrhythmias
LIDOCAINE.rationale: It prefers inactivated channels in depolarized tissue. Toxicity is neurologic, with perioral numbness and seizures.

CIRRHOSIS.clue: Bridging fibrosis and regenerative nodules that raise portal pressure and lower synthetic function
CIRRHOSIS.rationale: Albumin falls and the INR rises. Spider angiomas and gynecomastia reflect estrogen that the liver no longer clears.

EMPHYSEMA.clue: Alveolar-wall destruction with high compliance and low diffusing capacity
EMPHYSEMA.rationale: Smoking causes centriacinar disease at the apex. Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes panacinar disease at the base.

NEPHROTIC.clue: Protein loss above 3.5 grams per day with edema, low albumin, and high lipids
NEPHROTIC.rationale: Antithrombin III is also lost, so renal-vein thrombosis occurs. Infection rises because immunoglobulins leak.

ACHALASIA.clue: Failure of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax because inhibitory neurons in the myenteric plexus are gone
ACHALASIA.rationale: The barium column narrows like a bird's beak. Chagas disease can cause the same picture, and cancer risk is increased.

TAMPONADE.clue: Compression of the heart with hypotension, distended neck veins, and muffled sounds
TAMPONADE.rationale: Pulsus paradoxus and electrical alternans support the diagnosis. Diastolic pressures equalize, and drainage is the treatment.

PARKINSON.clue: Resting tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia from loss of pigmented substantia nigra neurons
PARKINSON.rationale: Lewy bodies of alpha-synuclein are the inclusion. Dopamine replacement helps motor symptoms; typical antipsychotics worsen them.

GONORRHEA.clue: Gram-negative diplococcus that ferments glucose only and causes purulent arthritis and neonatal eye infection
GONORRHEA.rationale: It grows on Thayer-Martin agar and has no polysaccharide capsule. Treat partners, and cover possible chlamydial coinfection.

COBALAMIN.clue: Vitamin whose lack causes megaloblastic anemia plus dorsal-column and corticospinal injury
COBALAMIN.rationale: Intrinsic factor from parietal cells and an intact terminal ileum are required for absorption. Methylmalonic acid is high, unlike in folate deficiency.

AQUAPORIN.clue: Water channel inserted into the collecting-duct membrane when vasopressin raises cAMP
AQUAPORIN.rationale: The V2 receptor drives that insertion. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus can be a mutant channel or a mutant receptor.

XERODERMA.clue: Nucleotide-excision-repair failure that leaves ultraviolet dimers and causes early skin cancers
XERODERMA.rationale: It is autosomal recessive. The cells cannot remove thymine dimers the way normal skin does.

LORAZEPAM.clue: Benzodiazepine preferred in liver disease because it is glucuronidated and has no active metabolite
LORAZEPAM.rationale: It increases how often the GABA-A chloride channel opens. It is a first drug for status epilepticus and alcohol withdrawal.

ISONIAZID.clue: Antitubercular drug that blocks mycolic acid synthesis and depletes vitamin B6
ISONIAZID.rationale: Hepatitis, peripheral neuropathy, and a lupus-like reaction are the classic toxicities. Pyridoxine is given to protect the nerves.

CLOZAPINE.clue: Antipsychotic reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia because it can wipe out neutrophils
CLOZAPINE.rationale: Seizures, myocarditis, severe constipation, and metabolic syndrome are other risks. The neutrophil count is monitored on a registry.

LINEZOLID.clue: 50S antibiotic for MRSA and VRE that can cause serotonin syndrome and thrombocytopenia
LINEZOLID.rationale: It weakly blocks monoamine oxidase. The platelet drop usually appears after about two weeks.

REJECTION.clue: Hyperacute graft failure from preformed antibody, versus later T-cell injury and chronic fibrosis
REJECTION.rationale: The hyperacute form thromboses the organ on the table. Acute cellular injury can respond to immunosuppression; chronic scarring does not.

UBIQUITIN.clue: Small tag that marks cytosolic proteins for destruction by the proteasome
UBIQUITIN.rationale: The chain is built on lysine residues. Proteasome inhibitors used in myeloma block the disposal step.

PENICILLIN.clue: Beta-lactam that binds the transpeptidase proteins of the cell wall and blocks the final cross-link of peptidoglycan
PENICILLIN.rationale: It mimics D-ala-D-ala. Hypersensitivity and, for some members, interstitial nephritis are the immune toxicities.

VANCOMYCIN.clue: Glycopeptide that binds D-ala-D-ala and is given orally only when the target is in the gut lumen
VANCOMYCIN.rationale: Too-rapid infusion releases histamine. It covers MRSA, and enterococci that swap in D-ala-D-lac are resistant.

GENTAMICIN.clue: Aminoglycoside that misreads the 30S subunit and is toxic to ear and kidney
GENTAMICIN.rationale: Killing is concentration dependent and needs oxygen, so anaerobes are not covered. A beta-lactam plus this drug is synergistic for enterococcal endocarditis.

AMIODARONE.clue: Multichannel antiarrhythmic that contains iodine and can scar the lung, inflame the liver, or swing the thyroid
AMIODARONE.rationale: Corneal microdeposits are nearly universal. The half-life is weeks, and it interacts with warfarin and digoxin.

KARTAGENER.clue: Dynein-arm defect with situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis
KARTAGENER.rationale: Primary ciliary dyskinesia also causes infertility because sperm and fallopian cilia do not beat. The chest infections are with the usual airway organisms.

DYSTROPHIN.clue: Sarcolemmal protein lost in frameshift deletions that cause early calf pseudohypertrophy and cardiomyopathy
DYSTROPHIN.rationale: In-frame deletions of the same gene cause a later, milder phenotype. Inheritance is X-linked and the creatine kinase is very high.

PLASMODIUM.clue: Intraerythrocytic protozoon transmitted by the Anopheles mosquito
PLASMODIUM.rationale: Falciparum makes multiple rings, high parasitemia, and cerebral disease. Vivax and ovale leave liver hypnozoites that primaquine eradicates after G6PD is checked.

DIPHTHERIA.clue: Phage-encoded toxin that ADP-ribosylates elongation factor 2 and creates a pharyngeal pseudomembrane
DIPHTHERIA.rationale: The heart and nerves are injured by the toxin, not by invasion. Antitoxin plus antibiotic is the treatment, and the vaccine is a toxoid.

COLCHICINE.clue: Microtubule inhibitor used for acute gout and familial Mediterranean fever
COLCHICINE.rationale: Diarrhea is the dose limit. Neutropenia and myopathy occur, especially if CYP3A4 inhibitors or kidney failure raise the level.

MYASTHENIA.clue: Fatigable ptosis and proximal weakness from antibodies against the postsynaptic acetylcholine receptor
MYASTHENIA.rationale: A thymoma or thymic hyperplasia is often present. Strength improves with an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor and worsens with use, the opposite of the Lambert-Eaton pattern.

SEQUESTRUM.clue: Island of dead bone inside chronic osteomyelitis
SEQUESTRUM.rationale: Periosteal new bone forms a shell around it. Staph aureus is the usual organism unless a special host, such as sickle cell disease, points elsewhere.

TOXOPLASMA.clue: Cat-associated protozoon that causes multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions when CD4 cells are very low
TOXOPLASMA.rationale: Congenital infection produces chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial calcifications. Treatment is pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, and leucovorin.

PEROXISOME.clue: Organelle that oxidizes very-long-chain fatty acids and synthesizes plasmalogens
PEROXISOME.rationale: Zellweger syndrome is a biogenesis failure with hypotonia and a large liver. X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy stores the same fatty acids and adds adrenal failure.

FLUMAZENIL.clue: Competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine site that can precipitate seizures
FLUMAZENIL.rationale: It does not reverse barbiturates or alcohol. Re-sedation follows because it is short acting, and it is avoided when a benzodiazepine was treating convulsions.

OMEPRAZOLE.clue: Irreversible blocker of the parietal-cell hydrogen-potassium pump
OMEPRAZOLE.rationale: It is a prodrug activated in the acid canaliculus and is taken before meals. Long use is linked to low magnesium, low B12, and Clostridioides difficile.

CONJUGATED.clue: Water-soluble bilirubin fraction that enters urine and rises when bile cannot leave the liver
CONJUGATED.rationale: The direct assay measures it. Dubin-Johnson and Rotor syndromes and extrahepatic obstruction raise it; hemolysis raises the insoluble fraction instead.

EPINEPHRINE.clue: Catecholamine of anaphylaxis that tightens vessels through alpha receptors and opens airways through beta-2
EPINEPHRINE.rationale: Intramuscular injection in the thigh is the first drug for anaphylaxis. Low doses favor beta-2 vasodilation; high doses favor alpha constriction.

VASOPRESSIN.clue: Posterior pituitary peptide that constricts vessels at V1 and inserts water channels at V2
VASOPRESSIN.rationale: V2 stimulation also releases von Willebrand factor from endothelium. Deficiency causes central diabetes insipidus; excess causes the syndrome of inappropriate secretion.

SARCOIDOSIS.clue: Noncaseating granulomas with bilateral hilar adenopathy and hypercalcemia
SARCOIDOSIS.rationale: Macrophages in the granulomas express 1-alpha hydroxylase, so calcium rises. ACE can be elevated, and the lungs, eyes, and skin are commonly involved.

KLINEFELTER.clue: 47,XXY primary hypogonadism with tall stature, gynecomastia, and azoospermia
KLINEFELTER.rationale: A Barr body is present. Testosterone is low, FSH and LH are high, and breast cancer risk is higher than in other men.

GOODPASTURE.clue: Autoantibody against glomerular and alveolar basement membrane with linear IgG
GOODPASTURE.rationale: The antigen is a type IV collagen chain. Lung hemorrhage plus rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis in a young smoker is the picture, and treatment is plasmapheresis plus immunosuppression.

CLINDAMYCIN.clue: 50S lincosamide used for anaerobes above the diaphragm and to shut off streptococcal toxin
CLINDAMYCIN.rationale: It covers many MRSA skin infections. The classic adverse association is Clostridioides difficile colitis.

PSEUDOMONAS.clue: Obligate aerobe whose exotoxin A ADP-ribosylates EF-2, seen in burns, cystic fibrosis, and puncture wounds through a shoe
PSEUDOMONAS.rationale: Pyocyanin makes the blue-green pigment and generates oxidants. Ecthyma gangrenosum marks bacteremia in neutropenia.

SCHISTOSOMA.clue: Blood fluke whose eggs, not the adult worm, drive portal hypertension or bladder squamous cancer
SCHISTOSOMA.rationale: Mansoni and japonicum eggs embolize to the liver, while haematobium eggs scar the bladder. Snails are the intermediate host, and praziquantel is the drug.

ALLOPURINOL.clue: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor used to prevent gout and tumor-lysis urate nephropathy
ALLOPURINOL.rationale: It raises azathioprine and mercaptopurine levels because those drugs share the enzyme. Severe rash is associated with HLA-B*5801.

DOXORUBICIN.clue: Anthracycline that generates oxygen radicals and causes dose-dependent dilated cardiomyopathy
DOXORUBICIN.rationale: It intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II. An iron chelator can limit the heart injury, and the urine may turn red.

HYDRALAZINE.clue: Arteriolar vasodilator that causes reflex tachycardia and a lupus-like syndrome in slow acetylators
HYDRALAZINE.rationale: It is used for hypertension in pregnancy and, with a nitrate, in some patients with systolic heart failure. The drug-induced lupus has antihistone antibodies.

FLUCONAZOLE.clue: Azole that blocks fungal 14-alpha demethylase and is used for Candida and cryptococcal maintenance
FLUCONAZOLE.rationale: It inhibits CYP enzymes. It does not treat Aspergillus or Candida krusei, and voriconazole is the mold drug instead.
